method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Changed tablet strength supplies a meaningful cause for the alert; comparison with the current order is the defensible verification step.
Documented disposal and prompt replacement preserve controlled-drug accountability and timely analgesia; false administration and delayed replacement are distinct errors.
Stable blood pressure permits clarification of possible undocumented administration before duplicate dosing; vital signs cannot reconstruct administration history.
1.8 mL with 5-mL cup graduations requires finer calibrated oral equipment; the dose provides discrimination.
Early emesis does not establish zero absorption; drug-specific guidance avoids unsupported full or half replacement.
Assessing tolerability while respecting refusal addresses the actual barrier and correctly distinguishes isolated nausea from allergy.
Discard key is sound, but keeping a vial attached to a needle for easier access is a weak implausible distractor.
issues: Discard key is sound, but keeping a vial attached to a needle for easier access is a weak implausible distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option 2 with: Withdraw the evening dose into a labelled syringe for bedside storage. Explain that future preparation/storage requires approved pharmacy processes rather than repurposing opened single-dose supply.

Old-patch check plus application documentation address duplication; alternatives leave exposure, irritation or memory risks.

Independent original calculations followed by comparison preserve independence; prior dose, pump movement and revealed answer do not.

issues: Stem calls medicines compatible, while distractor rationale argues mixture compatibility is not established. This can imply the very fact the explanation denies.

items.assessment: New renal decline plus a renally eliminated drug and drowsiness support accumulation despite unchanged administration; no independent dose adjustment is advised.
Increasing sedation after combination therapy merits assessment before further doses; respiratory rate alone is insufficient reassurance.
Post-infusion timing invalidates trough interpretation; reporting actual times enables an authorized sampling/dosing decision.
Medication-name recall is irrelevant filler; sleepy client needs sufficient arousal/swallow safety before oral trial is clearly defensible.
issues: Medication-name recall is irrelevant filler; sleepy client needs sufficient arousal/swallow safety before oral trial is clearly defensible.
proposedChanges: Specify that the client wakes easily, remains alert during conversation and has no swallowing restriction. Replace option 2 with: Measure the respiratory rate as the only evidence of nausea relief. Explain that this is a safety assessment rather than the intended antiemetic outcome.

items.assessment: Stable client and unknown Y-site compatibility support verification before co-infusion; speed and appearance cannot establish chemical safety.
Detached label with similar solutions makes physical tracing necessary; position, volume and prior diagram are unreliable proxies.
New resistance with pain requires stopping use and assessing complication; smaller syringe pressure and force are clinically meaningful common errors.

Vein-tracking warmth/tenderness favours phlebitis over cool swelling or adhesive-pattern reaction. Fluid overload is weak but still a recognizable IV complication differential; foundation metadata is more appropriate than application.
Sublingual dissolution preserves intended route; swallowing, mixing and chewing are recognizable administration misconceptions. Foundation metadata would be more accurate.
Observed coordination difficulty with adequate strength supports a compatible spacer and return demonstration, while device changes require assessment.
Labelled enteral equipment plus tracing addresses both identity and route risk; other options rely on position or omit identification.
Prompt supply coordination and escalation fit time-critical therapy without independent schedule or therapeutic substitution.
Correct key is defensible but elbow occlusion does not compete with management of the new facial rash and is topic-divergent.
issues: Correct key is defensible but elbow occlusion does not compete with management of the new facial rash and is topic-divergent.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: Use a weaker steroid left from a previous prescription on the facial rash. Explain that prior supply does not establish the diagnosis or current treatment authorization.
